Okay, let's tackle this. So I need to figure out which of the four options has a different conceptual meaning or thematic message from the others. All right, first step is to analyze each one individually. Let me start by reading them carefully and understanding their meanings.

Option 1: "همت اگر سلسله جنبان شود - مور تواند که سلیمان شود"  
Hmm, translating this... "If the will (همت) becomes the chain of [something], the ant (مور) can become Solomon (سلیمان)." Wait, Solomon is a wise king in Islamic tradition, often associated with strength and wisdom. So the metaphor here is that even a small creature like an ant can achieve the status of a great king if their will is in the right direction. The message seems to be about the power of determination or will to elevate one's status, regardless of their initial position. Like, if you have the right mindset or effort, you can rise to greatness.

Option 2: "گر پر پرواز بخشیدت فلک - همتی کن بال بگشا تا ملک"  
"Once the wings of flight are given to the sky (فلک), the will (همت) must stretch the wings to reach the kingdom (ملک)." This is a bit tricky. "فلک" here might mean the sky or the heavens, and "ملک" is kingdom. The idea is that if you have the wings (ability) to fly, then you should use your will (effort) to spread your wings and reach the kingdom. So again, it's about using one's will and ability to achieve a higher goal, maybe spiritual or worldly. The message is similar to option 1: determination leads to success.

Option 3: "هیچ کاری بی کمان نگشاید از تیر خدنگ - با جوانی همتی از پیر می باید مرا"  
This one is a bit more complex. "No work can be shot without a bow from the arrow of the heart (خدنگ might be a typo, perhaps خدنگ is خداغند? Or maybe it's a specific term I'm not familiar with). Wait, "تیر خدنگ" could be "arrow of the heart" or "arrow of the soul." The second line: "With youth, the will must be from the old to me." Maybe it's saying that even if you're young, you need the wisdom of the old (کمان is bow, so perhaps the bow is the wisdom or experience of the old). So the message here is that without the guidance or experience (the bow), even a young, eager will (arrow) can't achieve much. It's emphasizing the importance of experience or guidance in achieving one's goals through will. Still, the core idea is that will and guidance lead to success.

Option 4: "همتم هست رسا دستم اگر کوتاه است - ناتوان مورم و تا ملک سلیمان رفتم"  
"If my will is enough but my hands are short (limited), my ant (weakness) has become a Solomon and reached the kingdom." Here, the person is saying that even if their physical ability (hands) is limited, their will is sufficient to overcome that, and thus their weak self (ant) has become as great as Solomon. This is again about willpower overcoming limitations. 

So looking at all four, options 1, 2, and 4 all seem to be about the power of will (همت) and determination to achieve great things, even if one is weak or has limited means. They use the metaphor of an ant becoming Solomon, using wings to reach the kingdom, etc. The common theme is that strong will can lead to significant accomplishments, possibly even transcending one's natural state.

Now, option 3: It says that no work can be done without the bow (کمان) from the arrow of the heart. The second line talks about youth needing to take the will from the old (پیر). So here, the emphasis is on the necessity of guidance or experience (the bow from the old) for the young to achieve their goals. Unlike the others, which focus on willpower alone being sufficient, this one adds that without the right guidance (the bow), even the will can't do much. The message is that will and guidance are both necessary, or that youth needs the wisdom of the old. So this is a different concept because it's not just willpower but also the need for guidance or experience. The other options don't mention needing guidance from others; they focus more on the will itself being the key. 

Therefore, option 3 is the one that deviates because it introduces the idea that will alone isn't enough—you need the bow (guidance) from the old. The rest are about willpower leading to success regardless of initial conditions.
